nta.declaration: const int MIX = 6; // recipe MixSeconds const int INSP = 3; // inspection const int T_batter = 25; // timing.BatterWait: batter waits at most this for depositing to work again (FC7) const int POLL = 1; // BAT-INSP looks at the state once a second, so it really discards after T_batter + POLL const int LOST = 120; // bat.batchLostAfter: dosing gives up a batch that is not finished by now const int T_hb = 5; // timing.Heartbeat const int STALE = T_hb + 1; // BAT-INSP's copy of the state is at most one heartbeat plus one delivery old (estimated) const int BLOCKMAX = 60; // depositing may stay stopped this long (estimated) const int DEPSTART = 24; // a queued batter waits at most this for depositing to take it up: it may sit behind the previous batch, PansPerBatch 24 x depositTime 1 s clock g; // age of the batch clock h; // time since the inspector approved the batter bool stopped = false; // depositing is really stopped bool seen = false; // BAT-INSP's copy of that state bool queued = false; // "Batter ready" has reached depositing bool faultDone = false; // one stop only bool rejectDone = false; // one rejection only, the same one-fault bound as faultDone bool deposited = false; bool handedWhileStopped = false; // the real state at the instant of the handoff, not later: see FINDING 1 chan ready; // Batter ready (reliable, no acknowledgement)

template.name: Batch
template.declaration: clock x; int[0, T_batter + POLL] waited;

transition.label: x >= POLL && seen && waited + POLL <= T_batter
waited = waited + POLL, x = 0

query.comment: no deadlock (weak here: Copy never stops, so `deadlock` is unreachable whatever the stations do, see the two LIMIT queries)

query.formula: A[] Batch.Discarded imply Batch.waited <= T_batter + POLL
query.comment: T-RC4: a discarded batter waited exactly T_batter + POLL = 26 polls, derived from the loop and not asserted anywhere (tight: the same query with <= 25 fails). Counted on `waited`, not on a clock: Discarded is terminal, so any clock keeps running after the batch has ended

query.formula: A[] Batch.Holding imply h <= T_batter + POLL
query.comment: T-RC4: and it never waits longer than that before the handoff

query.formula: A[] (Batch.Mixing || Batch.Inspecting || Batch.Holding) imply g <= 2 * (MIX + INSP) + T_batter + POLL
query.comment: BAT's side of the batch is finished within 2 * (MIX + INSP) + T_batter + POLL = 44 s: one mixing cycle, one rejected cycle, and the full hold

query.formula: A[] (Batch.Mixing || Batch.Inspecting || Batch.Holding) imply g <= LOST
query.comment: T-RC6: and so well before the LOST limit

query.formula: A[] Dep.Took imply g <= 2 * (MIX + INSP) + 2 * DEPSTART + BLOCKMAX
query.comment: T-RC6: a batter is deposited at the latest 2 * (MIX + INSP) + 2 * DEPSTART + BLOCKMAX = 126 s after the batch was started (tight: 125 fails)

FINDING: T-RC6 is broken by a single rejection. 126 s is past dosing's LOST limit, so a batter can be deposited for a batch dosing has already given up (FC27) and replaced. Set rejectDone = true in the declarations and this becomes NOT satisfied, so the rejection is the whole cause

query.formula: A[] Dep.Took imply h <= 2 * DEPSTART + BLOCKMAX
query.comment: from approval to deposit at most DEPSTART + BLOCKMAX + DEPSTART (108 s), more than T_batter
deposited and discarded exclude each other
every inspected batch ends, handed over or discarded
a queued batter is always taken up in the end
FINDING: the state copy can be stale, a batter is handed to depositing at a moment when it is really stopped (unreachable if the state signal arrives without delay)
FINDING: after the handoff nothing limits the wait, a batter is deposited more than T_batter + POLL after approval (the exact maximum is 108 s: A[] Dep.Took imply h <= 107 fails, h <= 108 holds)
LIMIT: both stations can be frozen for good after a discard, which `not deadlock` above does not see
